newsitem.title: UK: Jupiter winds rage up to 600 kph -- scientists.
newsitem.headline: Jupiter winds rage up to 600 kph -- scientists.

text.p: Winds on Jupiter, the largest planet in the solar system, are stronger than originally believed and can rage at up to 600 kph (375 mph), U.S. scientists said on Wednesday.
They came to this conclusion after analysing data transmitted back to Earth in December 1995 by the Galileo probe, sent to the planet by the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA).

The scientists, led by David Atkinson of the University of Idaho, wrote in the British scientific journal Nature that wind speeds in the top clouds of Jupiter's thick atmosphere were around 90 metres a second or 325 kph (205 mph).
But they speeded up to almost twice that velocity as Galileo moved closer to the core of the largely gaseous planet.
The researchers said the reason for the high winds close to the planet's hot inner core was not clear.
"Whether these winds are driven by internal heat or absorbed sunlight remains uncertain," they wrote.
